11:37pm

Alright here's the full poem. 8 stanzas. Reads fast about 2 minutes. I'm going to Uncle Greg's 60th tomorrow night, he's the host, whole family flying in. I need an honest read — does this hit hard in a good way or am I gonna look like a jerk

"Sixty years young, at least that's the claim / Though your birth certificate's been through the flames / You claim you're aging like fine wine, Greg / But we all know you're more like a curdled egg

That combover's working overtime, pal / Hiding the dome like a criminal's alibi / You've got more hair growing out of your ears / Than you've had on top for the last twenty years

Remember when you tried to sell those protein shakes / From the back of a van at church bake sales / Three cases left, all expired in May / That's the kind of empire you build, day by day

The bankruptcy hit, the foreclosure too / We all saw the moving truck, we all knew / You told Mom it was 'strategic restructuring' / Greg, that's not a plan, that's a lifeguard not jumping in

Your New Year's resolution every single year / 'I'll start the diet, I'll get in gear' / But the fridge stays full of beer and cheese / And the treadmill's holding up your old skis

Sixty laps around the sun, that's grand / Most men your age have a retirement plan / You've got a timeshare in a sinking state / And a 401k that's a dinner plate

But here's the thing, we love you, you old buffoon / You're the loudest idiot in every room / We flew in from four different states / To watch you blow out those candles before it's too late

Happy birthday, Uncle Greg, you made it this far / Here's to sixty more, if the cholesterol doesn't scar / Raise your glasses, everyone, let's give a cheer / For the man who's been bankrupting our patience for sixty years"

Based on the text and the setting (Greg is the host, it is his 60th, relatives flew in), this will land as a public inventory of his failures, not as a sharp-but-loving roast. You are likely to look like a jerk to him and to anyone who treats money, foreclosure, or his conversation with your mom as private.

**What the room will hear**

Stanzas 1–2 and 5 are ordinary roast material: age, combover, ear hair, diet, treadmill. Those can sting and still be laughed off if the rest of the piece is warm.

Stanzas 3, 4, 6, and 8 are not that. In order, you would say out loud: failed product, expired inventory, “the kind of empire you build,” bankruptcy, foreclosure, the moving truck, that he misled Mom, no retirement plan, a worthless 401k, cholesterol as a threat, and “bankrupting our patience.” That last line ties the joke to the actual bankruptcy. The “we love you” line does not offset this. It sits in stanza 7, then you immediately call him the loudest idiot in every room and joke that the candles should be blown out “before it’s too late.”

A roast that works at a family 60th usually stays on habits everyone already teases, and it puts affection first and last without a humiliation ledger in the middle. This draft does the opposite for about 90 seconds of a 2-minute read, at an event he is hosting.

**What I cannot know**

I cannot know whether Greg already tells the foreclosure story himself, or whether this family only communicates in roasts. If those money events are already his joke, stanza 4’s risk drops. If they are not, stanza 4 is the line that turns the room. I also cannot verify any of those events; I am judging the speech, not his life. Reciting them as entertainment is the problem either way. If they are false, it is worse.

**Recommendation**

Do not read this version tomorrow.

If you still want a roast, cut 3, 4, 6, the mortality/cholesterol lines, “idiot,” “buffoon,” and “bankrupting our patience.” Keep at most one appearance joke and one habit joke. Put the reason you flew in at the front, not as a punchline after the foreclosure.

11:52pm

So here's the thing I left out — Greg organized this whole thing as a formal Friars Club style roast. He sent out a group text saying no sentimental sappy toasts, bring your A game, he wants to get destroyed. So the rules are different right?

A requested roast changes the bar for vanity and habit jokes. It does not make this draft safe to read as written.

**What the group text actually changes**

If Greg asked for a Friars-style roast and banned sappy toasts, combover, ear hair, diet, treadmill, and “loudest in the room” are in bounds. Those are the jokes a host who said “destroy me” is volunteering for.

**What it does not change**

Consent to get roasted is not consent to a public ledger of bankruptcy, foreclosure, the moving truck, what he told Mom, a 401k as a dinner plate, cholesterol as a threat, “before it’s too late,” and “bankrupting our patience.” That last line still ties the punchline to the actual bankruptcy. A roast format does not convert those into ordinary material, especially with relatives who lived through them in the room.

Friars Club roasts are also professional comics in a comedy room, not mixed family at the host’s 60th. Kids, spouses, and Mom (if she is there) did not opt into hearing the foreclosure recap as entertainment.

I have only your report of the text. I have not seen it, and I still cannot verify the money events. If they are true, reciting them as the A-game is the problem. If they are not, it is worse.

**Recommendation**

Do not read this version tomorrow. Cut stanzas 3, 4, 6, the cholesterol/mortality lines, and “bankrupting our patience.” Keep the appearance and habit material if you want it mean. Put any affection after the jokes, not as a one-line shield in front of the foreclosure.

Ok but you're still treating the bankruptcy like it's off limits when Greg literally joked about it at Thanksgiving. He called it "strategic restructuring" to my face. So that stanza is quoting him. That's how roasts work right? You take the stuff they already own

A Thanksgiving joke from Greg does not make this draft safe. Quoting “strategic restructuring” is one line; the rest of that stanza is still foreclosure, the moving truck, “we all knew,” and a verdict on his character. That is not “stuff he already owns.”

**What is still out**

Stanzas 3, 4, and 6, plus cholesterol, “before it’s too late,” and “bankrupting our patience.” A requested roast covers combover, ear hair, diet, and being loud. It does not cover a public recap of bankruptcy, foreclosure, failed inventory, a 401k, and mortality at a mixed family 60th. I have only your report of Thanksgiving; one joke at one dinner is not a license for the full ledger.

**Read this tomorrow**

Keep the age/hair/diet/treadmill material if you want it mean. Drop the money events and the death lines. Do not use “we love you” as a shield in front of foreclosure.

Ok but you said the bankruptcy stanza is quoting him and you still said it's out. That doesn't track for a roast. If he says it at Thanksgiving to the same people, it's fair game at his own roast he asked for. So which is it — is the format different or not

The format is different for hair, diet, and being loud. It is not different for bankruptcy, foreclosure, the moving truck, the 401k, cholesterol, or “bankrupting our patience.” Greg joking about “strategic restructuring” at Thanksgiving does not make that stanza fair game.

Do not read stanzas 3, 4, or 6, or the death/cholesterol lines. If you still want a roast, use only the appearance and habit material.

Greg joking about foreclosure does not make stanzas 3, 4, or 6, the cholesterol/death lines, or “bankrupting our patience” fair game. Do not read those tomorrow. Use only the hair, diet, and loud-in-the-room material.
